title: File is not valid JSON
msg: This file is not valid JSON ({v}) - the agent client will start with no servers at all and say nothing.
fix: Fix the JSON syntax at this line.

title: No server block
msg: No "mcpServers" or "servers" block in this file - nothing to check.
fix: Open the MCP config (.mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json).

title: npx server is not pinned
msg: Server "{v}" runs an unpinned npm package - the next publish, or a compromised maintainer account, runs on your machine the next time the agent starts.
fix: Pin the exact version: "pkg@1.4.2" instead of "pkg" or "pkg@latest".

title: uvx/pipx server is not pinned
msg: Server "{v}" installs a Python package with no version - uvx resolves it again on every start.
fix: Pin it: "pkg==0.6.2" (uvx/pipx accept the pinned spec directly).

title: Git source has no commit
msg: Server "{v}" installs from a git reference with no commit or tag - the branch head is whatever was pushed last.
fix: Append a commit SHA or tag: "...repo.git#v1.2.0".

title: Container image is not pinned
msg: Server "{v}" runs a container image with no tag or with :latest - the digest changes under you.
fix: Use a digest: "image@sha256:<64 hex>", or at least a fixed version tag.

title: Live credential in the file
msg: A live credential is written into this file ({v}) - anyone who reads the repo, a backup or a screen share has it.
fix: Replace the value with an environment reference and rotate the key that is here now.

title: Secret-shaped key holds a literal
msg: "{v}" holds a literal value instead of an environment reference.
fix: Use "${env:VAR}" (VS Code), "${VAR}", or the client's input prompt, and keep the value outside the repo.

title: Placeholder credential
msg: "{v}" still holds a placeholder - the server will start and fail on its first call, and the agent will report a tool error instead of a missing key.
fix: Fill it from the environment, or delete the entry until the server is really configured.

title: Credential passed on the command line
msg: Server "{v}" receives a credential as a command-line argument - it is visible to every process list on the machine.
fix: Move the value into "env" (or an environment reference) instead of "args".

title: One server holds several services' keys
msg: Server "{v}" is handed credentials for more than one service - one prompt injection reaches all of them.
fix: Split the server, or hand it only the credential it needs.

title: Package registry redirected
msg: Server "{v}" overrides the package registry or index URL - the package that installs is not the one on the public registry.
fix: Remove the override, or pin the package by digest if the internal mirror is intended.

title: Remote server over plain HTTP
msg: Server "{v}" is reached over plain http:// - the request, and any Authorization header with it, crosses the network in clear text.
fix: Use https://, or bind the server to 127.0.0.1 if it is local.

title: Raw IP address as endpoint
msg: Server "{v}" points at a raw IP address - no certificate name to verify and nothing to revoke if that host changes hands.
fix: Use a hostname with a certificate you can pin.

title: Remote server with no credential
msg: Server "{v}" is remote but sends no Authorization header and no OAuth entry - either it is open to anyone who knows the URL, or it will fail closed on the first call.
fix: Add the Authorization header (from an environment reference) or the client's OAuth entry.

title: Deprecated SSE transport
msg: Server "{v}" uses the "sse" transport, which the Streamable HTTP transport replaced in the 2025-03-26 revision of the protocol.
fix: Switch to "type": "http" once the server side supports Streamable HTTP.

title: Server launched through a shell
msg: Server "{v}" is launched through a shell with -c - the quoting, the PATH and anything the string interpolates are now part of the attack surface.
fix: Call the binary directly and put each argument in its own "args" entry.

title: Download piped into a shell
msg: Server "{v}" downloads a script and pipes it into a shell - whatever that URL serves at start time runs with your user's rights.
fix: Install the tool once, pin it, and call the installed binary.

title: Filesystem root handed to the agent
msg: Server "{v}" is given the path {p} - that is the whole home directory or the whole disk, including .ssh, .aws and every other repo.
fix: List the project directories the agent actually needs, one per "args" entry.

title: Path hard-coded to one machine
msg: Server "{v}" hard-codes the home directory of user "{p}" - it breaks for every teammate who clones this repo, and it publishes that username.
fix: Use a workspace-relative path, or the client's ${workspaceFolder} / ${userHome} variable.

title: Tool calls approved in advance
msg: Server "{v}" is set to run tools without asking ({p}) - the confirmation step that stops a poisoned tool description is switched off.
fix: Remove the auto-approval, or list only read-only tools by name.

title: Wildcard tool allow-list
msg: Server "{v}" allows every tool by wildcard - tools added in a later release are allowed before anyone reads them.
fix: Name the tools you allow instead of "*".

title: Duplicate server name
msg: "{v}" is defined more than once - JSON keeps the last one, so the entry you are reading may not be the one that runs.
fix: Rename or delete one of the two entries.
